mechanical.notes: 12/12 suites. Console clean. THE QUESTION IS DIFFERENT FOR A CURVED SUBJECT: the four box assets spent their triangle budget on PART COUNT, so their optimization asked 'what is duplicated?'; this subject spends it on CURVATURE, so the question is 'at the resolution we are judged at, are the polygons VISIBLE?' — computable via the SAGITTA: a radius-R circle in N segments deviates R(1-cos(pi/N)) at each chord midpoint, times screen px/m (19891 at dpr4 under, the most demanding state) = faceting error in PIXELS. The answer came out BACKWARDS: at 64 segments the mounting ring showed 1.21 px and the body 1.16 px of faceting — visibly polygonal on the two largest circles — while the whole build was at 1.9% of its triangle budget. So the correct optimization RAISES tessellation: segments are now RESOLVED from radius against a 0.5 px target (arcSegments in dims.mjs), not fixed magic numbers, and re-derive if capture resolution changes. Not blind — the same solver LOWERED small pieces (lens 64->40, barrel 64->56) and raised ring/body to 104 and bubble to 96, redistributing toward the pixels. Cost 1.9% -> 3.2%. REAL DUPLICATION also removed: boxes did not go through the geometry cache (only cylinders and the hemisphere did), so the two identical yoke arms each reserved a BufferGeometry — now shared (14 -> 13 unique, cache holds 13); sharing costs nothing and, unlike instancing, keeps meshes named/addressable for the hotspots and containment guards. Materials compared by FULL SIGNATURE (type/color/metalness/roughness/opacity/transparent/emissive/intensity/envMapIntensity/side/map), zero dups. NO instancing (nothing repeats enough; 13% of the draw budget; it would cost the named meshes hotspots+guards depend on), NO texture resize (measured both ways in surface), NO bubble decimation (spec-forbidden and measurement says it would be wrong). Verified: worst faceting 0.48 px; budget 15/120 draws, 8048/250000 tris (3.2%); 13 unique geometries cache-covered; artwork rasterises once; offline clean (orchestrator-verified: no fetch/XHR/WebSocket/Image/http, importmap -> ./vendor/three/); framing/optics 43-43/lighting/contrast/float/hotspot-reachability all unchanged. Silhouette confirmed smooth at dpr4 by orchestrator capture.

notes: Inline orchestrator judgment. A model optimization for a CURVED subject, and the instrument is the point: the sagitta turns 'are the facets visible?' into a pixel number, and it revealed the counter-intuitive answer — the two biggest circles were visibly polygonal at 64 segments while the build sat at 1.9% of budget, so the correct move was to RAISE tessellation (resolved from radius against a 0.5 px target) and REDISTRIBUTE down from the small pieces, the exact opposite of the box assets' remove-duplication pass. Real duplication (two uncached identical yoke arms) was still shared out, and instancing correctly declined to keep meshes addressable for the hotspots and guards. Silhouette is smooth at dpr4, offline clean, no regression. Cleared to P6 — after which the axis-camera asset is COMPLETE.
